current.text: He re-signed with Portland on a 3-year, 44 million USD contract.
He is the backup center behind Donovan Clingan, who is in Portland's projected starting five.
He outplayed Clingan in the playoffs.
The contract shows the team trusts him, but the expert does not expect him to start over Clingan.
He is expected to be capped at 17 to 18 minutes and to sit about 16 back-to-backs.
A Portland beat writer does not expect Clingan to play over 28 minutes.
Minutes and usage are expected to swing from game to game across Portland's rotation.
His 2P% jumped from 65 to 74 last season. The expert expects it to drop to about 68, which would cut into his FG% value.
At 23 minutes a night he would be a draftable category-league player.
Portland has three back-to-backs in our fantasy playoff weeks. Since he is expected to sit back-to-backs, this hurts him in the playoffs.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool.
He is a very efficient finisher on low volume. Twos drive most of his FG% value.
He makes almost no threes and scores little, even for a center.
His minutes and health are hard to trust.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 195, ESPN rank 166), so he will not be among our 144 drafted players and is a waiver name, not an auction target. His blocks (z +2.1 vs the pool), FG% and low turnovers fit punt PTS builds that want blocks, but a 17 to 18 minute cap, about 16 back-to-back rests and three Portland back-to-backs in our playoff weeks limit his weekly totals. Early in the season, watch Clingan's health and minutes: if Williams gets close to 23 minutes a night, he is worth adding.
